findings.title: Public findMany method removed without updating consumers
findings.body: The previous InsightsBookingService exposed a public findMany(findManyArgs) method that applied authorization and filter conditions while querying bookingTimeStatusDenormalized. This PR deletes it and only leaves getBaseConditions(); callers must now write $queryRaw manually. No production call site is updated in this diff, so any existing consumer of service.findMany will break at compile time or lose intended filtering. If the API change is intentional, callers must be migrated in the same change or the method retained.

findings.title: Constructor accepts weaker options type with optional teamId
findings.body: InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions declares teamId?: number independent of scope, and the constructor now accepts this type instead of the discriminated-union InsightsBookingServiceOptions. A caller can pass { scope: 'team', userId, orgId } and it now compiles; at runtime safeParse rejects it and the service silently returns the 1=0 condition, producing no rows with no error. This removes compile-time validation of required fields and can hide misconfigured call sites. The constructor should accept the discriminated union or a public type whose 'team' branch requires teamId.

findings.title: Caching behavior tests removed while caching code remains
findings.body: The diff deletes the Caching test block that verified getAuthorizationConditions and getFilterConditions are memoized on the service instance. The service still implements caching via cachedAuthConditions and cachedFilterConditions, including the null-vs-undefined handling for filters, but the new test file has no coverage for it. A regression that caches conditions for the wrong options/filters or mishandles a cached null filter result would go unnoticed. Restore equivalent caching tests adapted to Prisma.Sql return values.
